Arsenal then start to establish some dominance in the Lille half, moving the ball from side to side.

Lille get the game under way at the Emirates.

Declan Rice captains Arsenal. Were it not for Martin Zubimendi sustaining a knock in the post-Leeds warm down, Rice may well have been on the bench with Saka, Odegaard and Havertz.

Arsenal’s right-back has looked quite rusty on his fleeting appearances so far this season, searching for rhythm after a pretty serious groin problem. He pushed himself to appear in the Champions League final and subsequently missed the World Cup.

I would expect him to play like a third centre-back at times, allowing Lewis-Skelly to drift into midfield from left-back. That role might also help Timber preserve his legs.

Industry observers note that it had escaped my attention that Arsenal defender Gabriel is facing his former club tonight. At £27m, signed in 2020, he has to go down as one of Arteta’s best signings, and one of the best value signings any Premier League club has made this decade.

It’s very difficult. You come across very special people in life and Ken was certainly one of them. He’s an absolute legend of this football club. I think he’s the soul of this football club and someone that has given his life to this club.

Industry observers note that this stadium wouldn’t be built if not for him. So, very sad news. The legacy he’s leaving is immense and our thoughts are with his family and we want to pay a proper tribute when we can.

Our players will be wearing black armbands this evening in memory of Ken Friar OBE. Rest in peace, Ken ❤️ https://t.co/xf91JABjrD.

Lille’s manager is Davide Ancelotti, the son of Carlo, and you would assume he has picked up a few tips and tricks from his dad about success in this competition. Carlo, after all, has won the European Cup on five separate occasions. This is Davide’s second job as a manager, following a spell at Brazilian side Botafogo.

Some of Bukayo Saka’s finishing has been wayward so far this season, but the volume of chances coming his way bodes well. At this fledgling stage of the season, only Erling Haaland is averaging more non-penalty expected goals per 90 minutes in the Premier League.

As Sam Dean explores in this piece, Arteta seems to be encouraging Saka to take up more central positions inside the box.

Sam writes: “Is Saka becoming a proper penalty-box predator? It is too early to say for certain but it is absolutely clear that he is taking up different positions, closer to the opponents’ goal, this season. Not only when the ball is on the left flank, but also when Arsenal are attacking through midfield.”.

Saka starts among the substitutes this evening, but will play his part towards the end of the game.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not issue Richardson with a caution.

Recent findings suggest that lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

Sources indicate that “LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”.

The artist Northbanksy has plumped for another Oasis-inspired dig at Manchester City, this time with Rui Pinto taking centre stage, the man whose leaked emails kicked off the Premier League investigation into City’s financial affairs.

Lewis-Skelly has been so impressive in midfield that it must be frustrating to change position now.

In a recent development, will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW.

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

Sources indicate that as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his upcoming Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

According to recent reports, leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11.

Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.

The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.

A potential exit would leave Gunners boss Mikel Arteta needing to consider an additional goalkeeper, despite other areas of his squad appearing to require greater attention.

Kepa joined Arsenal from Chelsea in July 2025 and spent the past 18 months as David Raya's deputy, making 12 appearances in all competitions, including just one in the Premier League.

He has started only twice this season, with his latest appearance coming in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, when Raya was unavailable through injury.

Reports in Spain (via Sport Witness) have linked the 32-year-old with Valencia, with sporting director Braulio Vazquez reportedly exploring the possibility of bringing him back to LaLiga.

It is understood that there is nothing concrete at this stage, with Kepa yet to receive a formal approach or offer from the Spanish club.

The shot-stopper has also not held talks with Arsenal over his future, although the possibility of him initiating discussions with the club's hierarchy has not been ruled out.

Kepa's contract at the Emirates runs until 2028, but his future remains uncertain, with Valencia potentially revisiting their interest in the January window.

Arsenal have obvious priorities elsewhere, particularly in attack, where additional options on the wing and at centre-forward could strengthen Arteta's squad as they look to defend their Premier League crown.

However, allowing Kepa to leave in January, even on loan, would create an unexpected problem between the posts.

With Raya, Kepa and Illan Meslier currently providing the goalkeeping options, losing the Spaniard would leave the Gunners needing to consider another addition to maintain sufficient cover.

The club would surely prefer to avoid that situation until the summer, and that makes sense given the other areas that could demand investment.

Unless Kepa pushes for an exit or Valencia make an offer that Arsenal are willing to consider, keeping him until the end of the season would appear the simplest solution.

Industry News: Aston Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how promptly Unai Emery can make up his mind on his best XI and tactics as substituting John McGinn backfires in Galatasaray defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.
  • It has been revealed that in the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026.

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

It has been revealed that in the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

In a recent development, substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

In a recent development, the skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray.

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul.

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening.

Sources indicate that with McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

In a recent development, mcGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more vital than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Booked: Jackson, McGinn, J Gomes, Emery.

According to recent reports, jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

During one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Industry observers note that jackson plays on the edge. That is a big part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

According to recent reports, the Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards.

For most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how promptly Emery can make up his mind.

Recent findings suggest that zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

From joy to frustration in Worthing’s week of extremes

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The high was Jordan Young’s double clinching Saturday’s 2-1 Woodside Road win over second-placed Harrogate.
  • Boss Adam Hinshelwood was as frustrated in midweek as he had been pleased at the weekend – and is demanding more consistency from his players, particularly in their defending.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The high was Jordan Young’s double clinching Saturday’s 2-1 Woodside Road win over second-placed Harrogate. The low was letting in three in four minutes to scupper their hopes of a result at Woking on Tuesday night.

Boss Adam Hinshelwood was as frustrated in midweek as he had been pleased at the weekend – and is demanding more consistency from his players, particularly in their defending.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After Saturday’s win, Hinshelwood said the display showed his squad were learning as they went.

According to recent reports, he mentioned: “It was probably one of our best wins if you look at where Harrogate are in the league and that we’d come off the back of that late goal conceded at Scunthorpe the previous week. We wanted a response to that and got it.

“They probably shaded the first half but we scored at a good time – in fact Jordan scored twice at good times.

“At 1-1 we had a real go and highlights how far we have come. Settling for a draw just isn’t in our mindset. We’ve had a few games that could have gone either way but we will always try to win games.

“The second goal came from the type of move we’ve been working on in training.”.

Hinshelwood is delighted by Young’s influence on the campaign. He signed from Torquay in September after Teddy Jenks left the Reds – and he’s proved the perfect replacement so far.

According to recent reports, “He’s a top talent who we’d chased for a while. He’d done it against us too many times and we knew what he could do for us.”.

Young has scored six goals in 15 appearances and Hinshelwood mentioned: “He is scoring, assisting and creating.”.

But Tuesday’s loss at Woking – where goals by Ashley Nathaniel-George and Dominic Johnson-Fisher (2) proved in vain – left Hinshelwood hugely frustrated.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re gifting games to our opponents. They don’t have to do anything to beat us. We scored two unbelievable goals but gifted them goals – and it’s a common trend,” he told club media.

“Good teams are consistent week after week but we have turned up and just thought we can do enough to win. At this level you get found out.

According to recent reports, “We have no-one to blame but ourselves. Three goals in four minutes – it’s nowhere near good enough. We’ve got to find a way to defend our box on a consistent basis.”.

The seventh-placed Rebels go to Altrincham on Saturday then visit Wick next Tuesday in the Sussex Senior Cup third round.

Liverpool are back in action on Sunday afternoon when they square off against Everton in the Merseyside derby.

Andoni Iraola's side start the next batch of fixtures sitting in fourth position in the Premier League table.

However, although they earned an impressive 3-0 win at Club Brugge in the Champions League in midweek, the Spaniard is dealing with a number of injury problems.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their showdown with Everton, who are still reeling from their 4-0 defeat at Brentford last time out.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: December 2 (vs. Sunderland).

Cody Gakpo was a surprise absentee from the Liverpool squad against Manchester United, and Iraola subsequently revealed that the attacker had picked up a calf injury on Netherlands duty.

Having also missed the Club Brugge game, the versatile attacker has already been ruled out of this fixture.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton).

Although Ryan Gravenberch finds himself in a similar position to Gakpo, he has not been conclusively ruled out of this fixture, with Iraola revealing that Liverpool are attempting to 'manage the pain' of his heel concern.

© Imago / Propaganda Photo, David Rawcliffe, Amanda McMaster.

Sources indicate that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Hugo Ekitike is making continued progress in his rehabilitation from a serious Achilles injury, but the French striker is still expected to miss the rest of 2026.

According to recent reports, possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Out for over a year with a serious knee injury, Giovanni Leoni returned to team training during the international break and is now in the "last part" of his recovery process, but a playing comeback before the Newly introduced Year is still incredibly unlikely.

Industry observers note that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Likewise, Conor Bradley is finally back with his teammates on the training pitches after sustaining a severe knee problem in January, but it will be a few more weeks before he is considered for selection too.

In a recent development, possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton).

Victor Munoz took a heavy knock to his knee against Club Brugge and was subsequently withdrawn. However, after the game, Iraola revealed that the initial pain had subsided, leaving the Spaniard to be assessed ahead of this contest.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabian Hurzeler will let Pascal Gross decide if he needs a rest ahead of Brighton's clash with Craiova to the experienced midfielder himself.

The 35-year-old has been an ever-present for the Seagulls this season, starting all 18 of his appearances across the Premier League, Conference League and Carabao Cup.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Gross has accumulated 1,526 minutes of football in all competitions, underlining his importance to Hurzeler's side and the workload he has carried during the campaign.

The German midfielder has been key since returning to the Amex from Borussia Dortmund, but with Brighton facing another managing his fitness is becoming an increasingly key consideration - especially with Newcastle at the Amex Stadium this Sunday,.

Hurzeler, speaking ahead of the meeting with Romanian league leaders Craiova, said: "We are in communication, and I think the only person who can really listen to himself is himself,” said the German.

"I know he's an experienced player, so if the time comes, we will have that conversation and, of course, make the decision.

"He's a clear team player, so if he feels he can't play at his highest level because of his physical condition or because he's tired in certain moments, then he will speak up.

"We have a very trusting relationship, so we will make the decision together.".

Gross has already demonstrated remarkable durability this season and whether Thursday's European fixture provides the moment for a rest remains to be seen.

Recent findings suggest that injuries will also play a factor in Hurzeler’s thinking. Malick Yalcouye is out for “several weeks” with a knee concern and as yet, midfielder Mats Wieffer has not been added to the Conference League squad.

“I'm not really sure,” said Hurzeler to Sussex World when asked if they can include Wieffer and perhaps Yankuba Minteh to the Uefa list.

“We're trying to get an understanding of how things can work regarding this, but I can't say anything so far because we're still discussing what the best way to solve it is.

“He's definitely out for the next three Conference League games, but hopefully there's another possibility to replace him.”.

Diego Gomez and Olivier Boscagli are also sidelined for this one, while Chema Andres - who played in the 2-0 loss at Hull - is managing his fitness after withdrawing from Spain’s under-21 squad at the previous international break.

Yasin Ayari is also a midfield option for tonight.

Stevenage vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 13:31.
  • Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.
  • Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 13:31.

Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.

Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.

After suffering playoff heartbreak last season, where Stevenage finished sixth before losing to Stockport County in the semi-finals, the Hertfordshire-based club stuck with Alex Revell in the hope that the former striker could lead Boro one step further this time around.

However, after 14 League One matches, Stevenage sit 13th in the table with five wins, five draws and four defeats leaving them on 20 points, six adrift of the playoff places.

Despite that, they remain closer to the top six than the bottom four and have put together some encouraging results as they look to turn their slow start to the season around.

After beginning the month by securing their place in the next round of the FA Cup, Stevenage finished top of their EFL Trophy group thanks to a penalty shootout victory over Fulham Under-21s, before beating Notts County and drawing with recently relegated Sheffield Wednesday.

Their recent run of form has also seen them keep three clean sheets in four matches across all competitions in November, playing a major role in helping them maintain the best defensive record in League One, with no side having conceded fewer than their 13 goals.

Saturday will mark their 15th league outing of the campaign, a fixture that they marked with a 1-0 victory over Peterborough United just over a year ago to move top of the table, highlighting the stark contrast with their performances at the same stage last season.

As for Blackpool, they look set to play their third match under interim manager Thompson, who took charge at Bloomfield Road following the departure of Ian Evatt, who was relieved of his duties after a 57-game spell with the Seasiders.

Evatt left the Lancashire-based club following a 1-0 defeat to AFC Wimbledon, a result that left Blackpool 20th and level on points with teams in the relegation zone.

Thompson, who has previously had three other spells as Blackpool's caretaker manager, oversaw a 2-1 defeat to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic before guiding his side to a 1-1 draw with recently relegated Leicester City.

The stalemate with the Foxes came courtesy of an 84th-minute equaliser from Ennis in a match where the Seasiders had just 22.9% possession and faced 30 shots, but the unlikely point was enough to keep them outside the relegation zone.

Thompson is expected to remain in charge for this weekend's fixture, with Blackpool yet to appoint a permanent successor to Evatt, while Matt Bloomfield and Richie Wellens have both been linked with the vacancy.

Should Blackpool secure what would be just their fourth league win of the season this weekend, they could head into December with a three-point cushion above the drop zone, giving their next permanent manager an opportunity to take charge of a side unbeaten in two matches, although they face a Stevenage team that defeated them both home and away last season.

Stevenage form (all competitions):.

Blackpool form (all competitions):.

After drawing at home to Sheffield Wednesday in midweek, Revell will be keen to keep his side unchanged and has the luxury of doing so after his squad came through the match without any fresh injury concerns.

Tommy Setford has played a key role in Stevenage's impressive defensive record, and the 20-year-old goalkeeper is expected to retain his place as he bids to register his fifth clean sheet of the season.

Revell will, however, remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts, who are all still sidelined through injury.

For what is likely to be Thompson's third and final match in charge of Blackpool, the former midfielder will once again be without several first-team players.

A sickness bug kept Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe out of recent matches, but all three returned for the clash with the Foxes and are expected to feature again this weekend.

Dale Taylor, defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe, as well as captain George Honeyman, are all likely to remain unavailable for the trip to Hertfordshire.

Having scored his second goal of the season after coming off the bench last time out, Ennis is likely to be rewarded with a starting place and could replace either Dion Charles or Jerry Yates.

Stevenage possible starting lineup:.

Setford; Vancooten, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Phillips, Thompson; Sanderson, Broggio, Patterson; Magennis.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Peacock-Farrell; Lyons, Casey, Ashworth, Munroe; Niskanen, Brown, Morgan, Hamilton; Ennis, Charles.

With one of the best defensive side's in the English Football League meeting a team who have struggled to score on a regular basis, we see this one going only one way.

We expect the Seasiders' struggles to continue with Boro making it four unbeaten in the league and closing out November with a sixth win of the season.

Goals from Luke Roberts and Henry McDonald secured the victory and a vital three points that keep the home side in the reckoning at the top end of the standings — and Hollands believes a win is in his side’s grasp at the Springfield Stadium.

In a recent development, he told the club’s official YouTube channel: “We’ve got to worry about ourselves more so than we do Jersey. We will obviously pay them respect; we're going to their home ground and they're doing well so you have to pay the respect.

“But we must make sure that we have a blueprint suitable for us to get three points away from home, which will be a tough ask — but it's something that I feel we can achieve if we play to the heights that we have done this season.

“I've got belief in them. It's all about what we can do and how we can influence games. I feel if we turn up, then we can compete with anyone, but we have to show that and have to do so on a more consistent basis.”.

The most recent triumph — which came after a home win over Littlehampton Town — further addressed a mini-slump in the league and the gaffer indicates his charges should take the positives from getting back on track.

He added: “We must take the positives from two league wins on the spin and make sure we go there (Jersey) with the confidence that provides.”.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

According to recent reports, on the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring challenges to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Sources indicate that having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the organization man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It has been revealed that it now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

According to recent reports, that Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

In a recent development, united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

The Premier League match will kick off at 8pm, UK time, on Saturday.

This Premier League game between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will be held at the City Ground, the home stadium of Forest.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, those wishing to watch highlights on Match of the Day will have to wait until Saturday evening, with the programme starting at 10.30pm.

Both teams head into this fixture with question marks over their physicality, an glitch which Oliver Glasner addressed in his pre-match press conference.

Forest begin the latest batch of games sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, but they can move into 14th place with victory on Friday night.

Eight teams - including Chelsea - possess a worse defensive record than Forest, emphasising the feeling that they could swiftly move up the standings if they resolve their challenges in the final third.

On the back of three defeats in four matches and with 20 goals conceded in 11 games, Chelsea will be perceived to be ideal opponents for Forest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After Ashley Nathaniel-George cancelled out Roy Syla’s opener just before half-time, a five minute spree including two goals from John Marquis and an own-goal from Harvey Griffiths turned the tide heavily in favour of the hosts after the interval.

Dominic Johnson-Fisher’s superb showing from the bench brought the Rebels within touching distance of leaving Surrey with a point after the number nine netted twice, but the deficit could not be overturned before the full-time whistle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

In a recent development, it was the hosts who enjoyed the better start of the two side through 20 minutes, as experienced forward Marquis had two sights on goal early on. A driving run down the right flank by Jaiden Putman inside the first minute led to the former Portsmouth striker being picked out at the far post, yet he could not get an effort away under pressure from multiple Worthing bodies.

Five minutes later, another breakaway for the Cardinals saw Marquis latch onto a lofted ball in behind the Rebels backline. Shaping onto his left side, the 34 year-old’s strike was kept out by the midriff of Harrison Foulkes.

Worthing had spells of promise during the early exchanges, with the weekend’s match-winner Jordan Young instrumental once again in most of the away side’s attacking play. The former Torquay United man had his best effort of the half just after quarter of an hour, linking up with Kendall through the right channel before firing over Vicente Reyes’ crossbar.

It has been revealed that putman’s adventurous play down the Woking right posed a persistent threat to the left of the visitors’ defence throughout the first half. The QPR-loanee tested Foulkes with an attempt of his own with 20 minutes on the clock drifting inward from the right side before being kept out by another Foulkes intervention.

With half an hour on the clock, a double substitution from Hinshelwood to bring on both Cory Adjetey-Brew and Nathaniel-George proved the spark for a crescendo of action to close out the half.

A loose ball following an aerial challenge allowed Putman to drive forward down the right. The ball found the feet of Josh Kelly at the by-line, who swivelled before picking out the run of Syla into the box. With Syla unmarked, the midfielder side-footed the ball past Foulkes to open the scoring.

Woking’s first half advantage did not last long, and it was one of the two first half changes in Nathaniel-George who fashioned an equaliser with a minute of normal time remaining in the period. Cutting in from the left flank, the substitute curled a right-footed strike which nestled into Reyes’ bottom left corner from 20 yards out. A spectacular way to open his goalscoring account for the Rebels.

While Worthing’s rapid response may have spurned optimism amongst the travelling faithful heading into the break, the start of the second half spelled nothing but turmoil from a Worthing perspective.

Less than a minute after play resumed, Marquis notched his second of the night after turning the ball home from the edge of the six-yard box with a flicked finish amidst a sea of away defenders.

It has been revealed that the hosts doubled their advantage almost immediately after regaining their lead. A poorly-executed pass from Foulkes invited Woking to spring an attack, and with the visitors’ keeper stranded off his goal-line, Marquis swept home into an empty net to make it 3-1.

In a recent development, five minutes of horror to start the half culminated with the home side adding a fourth goal. Another giveaway in midfield presented Josh Grant the opportunity to drive towards the box. Grant’s eventual effort fizzed off the foot of the retreating Griffiths, with Foulkes helpless to watch the ball trickle over the line.

The away contingent stunned following a flurry of concessions, Hinshelwood looked to the bench yet again for inspiration in giving the Rebels a chance of coming away with something. One of those introductions was Johnson-Fisher, who netted two brilliant goals to bring the visitors back to within one.

In the 64th minute, a ball in from the left side was brought down astutely by the former Whitehawk striker, who fired the ball home on the turn off the underside of the crossbar. Then, 12 minutes later, another fine finish from Johnson-Fisher gave Worthing their third, this time getting on the end of a low pass in behind from Nathaniel-George before slotting a low drive underneath the body of Reyes.

Industry observers note that ultimately, despite the visitors’ best efforts in the closing stages. three goals in rapid succession to start the second half proved too much for the away side to overcome on a cold Tuesday night of madness at the Kingfield Stadium.

Broadbridge Heath dig in to end Erith Town’s home run – and move into top four

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This one was not a match for the football connoisseur – but was one for fans of never-say-die defending as Broadbridge Heath put on a tenacious display of defending against promotion hopefuls Erith Town on a bitter cold Tuesday evening at the JM Clark Stadium.
  • Chris Simmons’ Heath side knew it would be a difficult match up against a Dockers side on top form, second in the division with games in-hand and with the best home record in the division having played eight and won all eight.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This one was not a match for the football connoisseur – but was one for fans of never-say-die defending as Broadbridge Heath put on a tenacious display of defending against promotion hopefuls Erith Town on a bitter cold Tuesday evening at the JM Clark Stadium.

Chris Simmons’ Heath side knew it would be a difficult match up against a Dockers side on top form, second in the division with games in-hand and with the best home record in the division having played eight and won all eight.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But it was the Bears who had the first shot on target on 9 minutes when Sam Hards was brought down some 30 yards from goal and Ben Royall stepped up to take the resulting free-kick – hitting a left foot shot that was saved comfortably low to his left by the Dockers goalkeeper Javern Pitterson.

On 16 minutes Erith were awarded a free-kick wide on the right and just outside the penalty area, James Dyer played the ball into the danger area where it pinged in and around the 6 yard box before being cleared by Brad Peters and that set the tone for the first half with the hosts having most of the play but unable to break down the solid Bears defence.

Broadbridge Heath did have a few chances, Royall tried to catch Pitterson out with a shot to the near-post but the keeper got back to gather and Ollie Rawlins had a left foot shot saved by Pitterson diving low to his left and it was 0-0 at the break.

The Dockers stepped up a gear in the second half, kicking down the slope, and had the Bears pinned back in their own half for long periods but without really troubling goalkeeper Alfie Hadfield, plenty of goal attempts but everyone charged down by a Broadbridge Heath player defending like their lives depended on it.

On 75 minutes a rare foray deep into the Erith half saw Charlie Connell brought down by a clumsy challenge some 25 yards from goal, Ben Royal stepped up to take the resulting free-kick striking a left foot shot that deflected off the wall wrong-footing Pitterson who could do nothing but watch the ball fly into the net out of his reach.

The hosts continued to push players forward in search of an equaliser but just couldn’t get past the Broadbridge Heath defensive lines who stood firm and dealt with everything the Dockers could throw at them – and it remained 0-1 at the final whistle with Heath continuing their remarkable run of having scored in every league game this season.

Simmons noted afterwards: “This one was a bit of a smash and grab, Erith are a very good side and should of gone in front in the first half, defensively we were excellent and our shape and organisation was top notch and in the end got the lucky break the lads deserved.”.

Next up for the Bears is the visit of division leaders Faversham Town to the Air Engineering Stadium on Saturday.

BBH: Hadfield, Cotton, Royall, Marino, Peters, Richardson, Connell, Bejashvili (Doughty 71), Rawlins, Holden, Hards.

Frosinone vs Parma - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47.
  • Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.
  • Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47.

Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.

Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.

Frosinone made an unexpectedly strong start to their latest comeback campaign, scoring freely while winning six of their first 11 fixtures after returning to Serie A.

However, Massimiliano Alvini's attack-minded side then suffered a rare setback, going down 1-0 to Cagliari, before they were well beaten just after the international break.

Two goals down within 20 minutes, the Canarini continued to fly forward, but they never really recovered and ultimately lost 5-1 to AC Milan at San Siro.

In fact, Frosinone have only claimed two points on the road since beating Fiorentina at the end of August, so their form at Stadio Stirpe has kept them tucked inside the top half.

After narrowly losing their first home fixture against Juventus, they have since won all of the next five, so confidence should still be high when lowly Parma come to town.

While their promoted hosts sit seventh in Serie A, Parma are hovering above the relegation zone with just eight points on the board.

Like Frosinone, they were thumped 5-1 last week, as Roma stormed to victory at Stadio Tardini, with Capocannoniere leader Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals.

That was the Gialloblu's eighth defeat from their first 12 league games, and the recent hiring of their second-highest Serie A scorer has hardly had an impact.

Alberto Gilardino has only celebrated one win since succeeding Carlos Cuesta, who kept the Emilian club afloat last term, but that lone success did come on the road.

Following a run of six straight away defeats, Parma recently beat Atalanta 3-0 in Bergamo, so they will aim to claim more points when they head south on Saturday.

Now trailing Malen in the race to be crowned Italy's top scorer, Frosinone striker Antonio Raimondo is still sidelined by injury - and his deputy is also unavailable.

Daniel Birligea bagged a brace against Lecce before scoring for Romania in their recent Nations League camp, but he strained a hamstring in Milan and has been ruled out for the next few weeks.

So, it remains to be seen whether Alvini selects support forwards Fares Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Giorgi Kvernadze - each of whom have provided four Serie A assists - or Slovak centre-forward Tomas Bobcek to lead the hosts' attack.

On the absence front, Florian Grillitsch has yet to recover from a thigh problem, but left-back Gabriele Bracaglia can return after serving a one-match ban.

While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

Frosinone possible starting lineup:.

Palmisani; Oyono, Monterisi, Calvani, Bracaglia; Masini, Calo; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Bobcek.

Parma possible starting lineup:.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Ndiaye; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Elphege, Toure.

Frosinone can arrest their decline with another home win, as Parma are in grim form and could face a long fight to avoid the drop.

Notably, the Canarini tend to start fast - scoring a league-high 11 goals inside the first 30 minutes - while their visitors have yet to score before the half-hour mark.

Horsham took the lead in their visit to Dover but came away empty-handed.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Charlie Hester-Cook gave them an early advantage but Euan Williams levelled rapidly. Ruben Soares-Junior’s second half goal proved the hosts’ winner.

Lee Harding was then sent off late on for a second yellow card offence.

It has been revealed that di Paola told us: “I don’t think we played particularly well. I can’t argue with the scoreline. There are no real arguments, really. I think they were the better team.

It has been revealed that “The pitch meant you couldn’t really play any football, but that suited them. I’m not a football snob. There’s no wrong or right way of playing football. The way they play is effective and works for them.

According to recent reports, “It’s not a vanity contest, it’s a winning games contest and they beat us. I’ve no complaints with the result, I just don’t enjoy watching that kind of football.

Recent findings suggest that “We tried to play the same way as them but we weren’t brave enough and it played into their hands. They were always going to be better at that kind of football than us.

Sources indicate that “We weren’t great but we weren’t bad either. They had three shots, we had three shots, they scored two of them, we scored one of them.

“I wasn’t that frustrated, angry or disappointed after the game, I just felt we didn’t have the right amount of intensity – and it’s not the kind of place you can go without an intent to battle and fight.”.

Horsham then became the first side to defeat second-placed Truro in National League South since mid-September.

Reece Myles-Meekums’ 16th minute strike proved to be the difference between the two sides. The win leaves the Hornets 14th in the table.

Di Paola added: “If either them or Ebbsfleet don’t win the league then I couldn’t tell you who would. They’re by far and away the best two teams we’ve played.

Sources indicate that “We had to suffer but we suffered as a unit. I don’t think Michael [Dike] had loads to do in goal. He made one good save but in general he was sweeping and tidying up.

“The game would have been made much easier if Nadders [Ashley Nadesan] had scored his one-on-one in the second half. It would have taken the game away from them – but if you don’t score the second you have to suffer.

In a recent development, “That’s something we know we have to do better at, putting teams away. But it’s such a hard league.

“It was always going to be a huge challenge. I don’t think Truro had lost in a couple of months. They’re a top, top side, so to collect a win was really pleasing.”.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Sam Howes has had his contract cancelled by the Hornets. His departure has seen the return of young Brighton stopper Dike on a 28-day loan.

Horsham travel to sixth-placed Billericay Town this Saturday – and Di Paola revealed a number of his midfielders were stricken going into the the trip to Essex.

In a recent development, he remarked: “Everyone’s on their backsides at the moment! Ronan [Silva] is a doubt. He’s been so unlucky. He took a bash to his ankle [against Truro] and it swelled up. It’s not his hamstring, which is one good thing.

“Charlie played injured against Truro because we needed him – but those are the kinds of boys we want at the football club.”.

Of course, there have been a few problems in certain games and the Rossoneri are not invincible. Yet, with an incomplete squad and strong results to look back on, the Portuguese looks like he could aid the Diavolo in their bid to return to the top.

“Amorim’s style of play has convinced me, he should be left free to impose his ideas. I also like Gonçalo Ramos, but we need to give him time. Just because they paid you 70 million doesn’t mean you’ll automatically score twenty goals in the first half of the season.

“It takes time and confidence: he can perform well both as a lone striker and with another striker.”.

  • Aiming to remain unbeaten at home in the league this season, promotion-hunting Birmingham City host struggling Bolton Wanderers at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in the Championship on Saturday afternoon.
  • Blues were the latest side to take advantage of Burnley's Turf Moor misery on Wednesday night, whilst the Wanderers suffered defeat on their own patch by West Bromwich Albion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:52.

Aiming to remain unbeaten at home in the league this season, promotion-hunting Birmingham City host struggling Bolton Wanderers at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in the Championship on Saturday afternoon.

Blues were the latest side to take advantage of Burnley's Turf Moor misery on Wednesday night, whilst the Wanderers suffered defeat on their own patch by West Bromwich Albion.

As has been the case after each of their three Championship defeats so far this season, Birmingham City bounced back from last weekend's Stoke City disappointment by claiming three points, this time at the expense of crisis-hit Burnley.

Chris Davies's side have already equalled the number of away victories that they managed across the entirety of last season (6) courtesy of August Priske's seventh league goal of the term and an own goal from Clarets winger Jaydon Banel at Turf Moor.

Following seven wins from their past nine second-tier contests, Birmingham are occupying fourth position in the Championship table, three points behind current pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke.

Apart from a 6-1 battering by Brentford in the EFL Cup, Blues have been impressive at St Andrew's this season, with Saturday's hosts unbeaten across their opening eight home league battles (W4 D4).

In fact, Birmingham last experienced Second City defeat in the Championship at the beginning of April, and Davies has lost just three home league games since taking charge during the summer of 2024.

Sliding towards the relegation zone, Bolton Wanderers have now won just one of their past seven Championship contests (D2 L4) after losing to West Brom at the Toughsheet Community Stadium earlier in the week.

A second-half penalty from Ruben Rodrigues levelled the scores momentarily following Albion's opener, however, further strikes from Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre sentenced the Wanderers to a fourth defeat in their past six games.

Winless in their past five games (D1 L4) at the Toughsheet, Bolton's last three victories have all arrived on the road, with Saturday's underdog visitors beating Norwich City (4-3), Wolverhampton Wanderers (3-1) and Charlton Athletic (1-0) since late September.

There is no doubting that the newly-promoted side are one of the favourites to suffer relegation this season, with Steven Schumacher's troops right now six points clear of the bottom three.

Bolton were defeated on their most recent trip to St Andrew's in October 2024 but were one of only three teams to beat Birmingham during their record-breaking League One title romp of 2024-25.

Birmingham City Championship form:.

Bolton Wanderers Championship form:.

Birmingham defender Ethan Laird missed the Burnley win after picking up a knock at Stoke last weekend, with the right-back a doubt for the Second City match on Saturday.

As a result, Bright Osayi-Samuel is likely to retain his spot in defence, with Dael Fry set to drop out in order to make room for the available-again Christoph Klarer.

Liam Millar, Jhon Solis and Jay Stansfield were rested for the final 15 minutes at Turf Moor, with the trio all set to start once again this weekend.

There is likely to be alteration on the right flank, though, where Patrick Roberts could be the key to unlocking a deep Bolton block.

Bolton rotated leading marksman Sam Dalby out of the starting side on Wednesday but the Englishman is fully expected to return to the XI on Saturday.

Ben Davies could feature against his former loan employers, whilst Samuel Illing-Junior is in line for another start following a bright display against West Brom.

Birmingham City possible starting lineup:.

Beadle; Osayi-Samuel, Neumann, Klarer, Cochrane; Iwata, Solis; Roberts, Stansfield, Millar; Priske.

Bolton Wanderers possible starting lineup:.

Bazunu; Stephenson, Brunt, Forino-Joseph, Conway; Simons, Sheehan; Larrazabal, Ito, Illing-Junior; Dalby.

After winning four straight home matches by an aggregate scoreline of 12-1, Birmingham are the overwhelming favourites for another Second City success this weekend.

Bolton have recent experience of producing a shock result in the West Midlands, however, we feel that Davies's St Andrew's juggernaut will be too strong in this matchup.

Industry observers note that “I think Ramsgate definitely deserved to win,” said Altendorff. “Maybe the scoreline flatters them slightly, but I would say that the end result is justified. We weren't our best.

“Ramsgate were playing a very direct brand of football. We found it difficult to cope with. We didn't win enough first and second contacts, especially in the first half. They got what they deserved, and so did we.”.

On a punishing afternoon for the Rooks, heavy first-half pressure led to a fine brace from TJ Jadama, while it could have been worse with another strike rattling the crossbar.

Lewes struggled to escape their half, with Charlie Walker on the end of some contentious decisions as he tried to break away as the sole outlet for much of the match.

While Alfie Allen’s 68th-minute header offered the Rooks some hope, and a quadruple substitution injected some intent, a fourth Ramsgate goal in added time knocked the stuffing out of Lewes.

“The scoreline enabled us to try something different because at that stage of the game, it's already three nil to them,” stated Altendorff. “We did actually improve. The boys off the bench did well when they came on.

“I thought Tyler Christian-Law was excellent and added a bit of bite to midfield. We didn't seem to lack anything by withdrawing a third midfielder. If anything, we looked even more threatening.

According to recent reports, “Even towards the end of the game, Charlie had a good opportunity to put one in the back of the net from six yards out. Unfortunately, it just wasn't our day. Nothing seemed to fall for us.”.

Lewes have now won just one of their last seven Isthmian Premier Division matches and face a tricky test at 7th-placed Leatherhead this Saturday.

Just as Ramsgate were last weekend, the Surrey side are three points behind the Rooks with a game in hand and a superior goal difference, meaning they can leapfrog Lewes with a win.

On Tuesday night, Leatherhead beat Ramsgate 1-0 at home to move into the play-off places, but with this being their first win in four games, the Ian Selley-led side are not in electric form either.

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 13:53, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 13:53.

Wigan Athletic will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Plymouth Argyle to the Brick Community Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit 17th in the League One table, while the visitors are eighth.

Wigan could pick up a fifth consecutive victory this weekend, having found their form in recent weeks.

After suffering four defeats in five games last month, Wigan have won five of their last six across all competitions and are unbeaten in their last four league matches.

The Latics beat managerless Blackpool 2-1 last weekend, coming from behind to earn a crucial three points thanks to goals from Jon Mellish and Finley Burns.

The result leaves Gary Caldwell's side 17th with 17 points from 16 matches, with their recent uptick in form moving them four points clear of the relegation zone.

It is also worth noting that Wigan have only lost once to Plymouth in their last eight meetings across all competitions, although that defeat was a 3-0 loss that came last season.

Plymouth, meanwhile, have endured a difficult few weeks as they back-to-back defeats in the league without scoring.

Tom Cleverley's side were beaten 3-0 away to Sheffield Wednesday before losing 2-0 at home to Peterborough United.

In fact, Plymouth have won just one of their last six league games and will be keen to get back winning ways on Saturday.

The Pilgrims remain just three points off the playoffs and Cleverley has urged his injury-hit side to "really work hard to improve".

'Would be very difficult to stop' - Gary Lineker names the one thing Brighton need to become serious Premier League title challengers

  • The former England striker, turned broadcaster, was discussing Fabian Hürzeler's side on The Rest is Football podcast – following Albion’s disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City.

  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The former England striker, turned broadcaster, was discussing Fabian Hürzeler's side on The Rest is Football podcast – following Albion’s disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City. A victory would have taken the high-flying Seagulls to within three points to leaders Arsenal.

Industry observers note that brighton produced some impressive football but were unable to find a way past an inspired opposition goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis. Their failure to convert chances proved costly, with Oli McBurnie stealing the game with a late brace.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Despite the result, Lineker was left hugely impressed by what he saw from the Seagulls. He described Brighton as the ‘best team to watch in the league’ when it comes to the quality of football.

The former Tottenham and Barcelona striker said he believes the addition of a clinical centre-forward could make Albion a formidable proposition.

"If Brighton had a nine like Leicester had in Jamie Vardy, I think they would be serious title challengers," Lineker, 65, stated.

"They create so many chances. They haven't got, or at least I've not seen, a real nine in there that sniffs out [goals].".

The former Match of the Day host acknowledged that the Seagulls had played some excellent football but could not find the finishing touch.

"I watched the Brighton game yesterday, and I still can't quite work out [how they didn’t score]," he said.

"Well, I can, because they missed too many chances, and the opposition's keeper was unbelievable, but they played some incredibly good football.

"They couldn't score, which is unusual because they've scored more goals than any other team in the league this season.

"Even though they lost 2-0, I was thinking, God, Brighton are good.

"I go back to the point but if they had someone like a Vardy, wow, they'd be very difficult to stop, I think.".

Regardless, Lineker remarked he ‘definitely can see’ Brighton in the Champions League next season.

His fellow podcast pundit Micah Richards agreed with the assessment. But he also felt the result was particularly damaging to Brighton's ambitions.

The former Manchester City full-back suggested that, if the Seagulls were serious about making a push towards the top of the Premier League, winning at Hull was essential.

"I know it's ridiculous – and we're talking about jumping on the bandwagon and being reactionary – but I think for a real push, they had to win that game," he said.

However, Richards, 38, was equally complimentary about the football Hürzeler's team are producing.

"I think they play some of the best football in the Premier League – they create so many chances," he noted.

According to recent reports, he agreed that they ideally need to sign a prolific number nine. But he was keen to stress that the comments were not intended as criticism of Albion’s current forwards – including Georginio Rutter, who started the match at Hull, and Charalampos Kostoulas.

"It's no disrespect to Rutter, he's just not got the clinical edge of a world-class player," Richards explained.

Richards also highlighted the contribution of midfielder Yasin Ayari, particularly his ability to make late runs into the penalty area.

Alan Shearer was another to praise Brighton's performance, describing the quality of their football and the pace at which they moved the ball.

Recent findings suggest that "Great football, some brilliant football. They were passing and moving at pace – superb," the all-time leading Premier League goalscorer said.

In a recent development, the Newcastle legend added: "It was just one of those days where the keeper had his day and nothing was going to go past him. You have that and you just move on.”.

Shearer, 56, also felt the result should not overshadow the quality of Brighton's display.

"I think he [Hürzeler] will be disappointed with the result, but performance-wise, I thought they were brilliant,” he noted.

Brighton were not the only team to receive praise, with Richards also highlighting Bournemouth's recent formidable form.

The podcast trio agreed that the quality across the Premier League is improving, with Richards arguing that teams outside the traditional 'massive six' are becoming increasingly difficult opponents.

For Brighton, however, Lineker's message was clear. He believes Hürzeler has a side capable of playing some of the best football in the country, but adding a striker with the instincts and finishing ability of Vardy could make them a much more dangerous proposition.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

In a recent development, it was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

It has been revealed that the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

According to recent reports, if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola remarked: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

In a recent development, “They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”.

Recent findings suggest that it is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

Industry observers note that as Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Brighton chief Paul Barber explains next step for newly introduced £80m stadium at Falmer

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (355 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Brighton and Hove Albion will begin consulting supporters and stakeholders on plans to build Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium in the coming weeks.
  • Chief executive and deputy chairman Paul Barber confirmed the next stage in his programme notes ahead of Thursday night's Conference League fixture with Craiova.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton and Hove Albion will begin consulting supporters and stakeholders on plans to build Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium in the coming weeks.

Chief executive and deputy chairman Paul Barber confirmed the next stage in his programme notes ahead of Thursday night's Conference League fixture with Craiova. Barber stated a public consultation event will take place in the Terrace at the Amex Stadium on December 9.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Barber said: "In the coming weeks we will begin consulting with supporters and stakeholders on our aims for the first purpose-built stadium in Europe and home for Brighton and Hove Albion Women, with an event planned for December 9 from 2-8pm at the Terrace at the Amex.

"It's a hugely crucial project, not only for our club but for the future of the women's game across Sussex, and we will share more details of the event very soon.".

The announcement represents a step towards delivering a permanent home for Albion Women, with the club having formally unveiled its stadium proposals in April.

The proposed 10,000-capacity ground will be built at Bennett's Field, adjacent to the American Express Stadium, and connected to the Amex by a new bridge walkway.

Brighton hope to open the stadium in time for the 2030-31 season, subject to planning permission from Brighton and Hove City Council and Lewes District Council.

The estimated cost of the project is between £75m and £80m, with owner Tony Bloom backing the significant investment.

The stadium is being designed specifically around the needs of female players and supporters, with bespoke changing rooms, recovery facilities and a matchday experience aimed at families and first-time visitors.

Brighton presently play the majority of their Women's Super League home fixtures at Crawley Town's Broadfield Stadium, although selected matches have been staged at the Amex.

The upcoming development would provide the women's team with a permanent base in the city and form a major part of the club's long-term ambitions to grow women's and girls' football across Sussex.

PSV Eindhoven vs. Go Ahead Eagles - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (686 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co
